# Dokkit

> Self-hosted monitoring that says what needs a look. A server you host, one small program on each machine, and one API behind everything.

An AI tool reaches Dokkit over MCP at `/mcp` on the server, or over the HTTP API, with a user token whose scopes decide what it may do.

## Docs

- [The API](https://dokkit.dev/api.md): every call, with what to send and what comes back
- [The command line](https://dokkit.dev/cli.md): every `dokkit` command
- [The API as OpenAPI 3.1](https://dokkit.dev/openapi.json)
- [Everything in one file](https://dokkit.dev/llms-full.txt): the API, the command line, the MCP tools and the `dokkit.toml` reference


# The MCP server

Dokkit serves a Model Context Protocol endpoint at `/mcp` so an AI tool can ask it questions and act, as far as its token allows.

It lives on the server, never on `dokkit`. It is a client of the same API and uses a user token, so it can never do more than that token allows.

## Connecting

Over HTTP with a user token as a bearer header. For Claude Code:

```
claude mcp add --transport http dokkit https://<dokkit address>/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer dku_..."
```

## Tools

| Tool | Scope | Does |
|---|---|---|
| `attention` | `read` | Shows what needs a look now, what will soon, what was found and is not watched, what is snoozed, issues in other environments, and how many things are fine. |
| `find` | `read` | Searches services, optionally on one machine. |
| `service` | `read` | Shows one service: state, checks, routing, open issue. |
| `since_deploy` | `read` | Shows what changed or broke for a service since its last deploy. |
| `jobs` | `read` | Lists jobs with their schedule and last runs. |
| `job_runs` | `read` | Lists the recent runs of one job. |
| `errors` | `read` | Lists error groups, or shows one with its stack. |
| `machines` | `read` | Lists machines. |
| `machine` | `read` | Shows one machine. |
| `issues` | `read` | Lists issues. |
| `issue` | `read` | Shows one issue with its history. |
| `deploys` | `read` | Lists recent deploys. |
| `versions` | `read` | Lists the versions of the apps Dokkit watches. |
| `rules` | `read` | Lists the alert rules. |
| `proposals` | `read` | Lists what Dokkit found and a person may accept or dismiss, each with `origin` and `why`. Leaves out the operating system's own things unless `system` is true. Always answers `{"items": [...], "next": ..., "hidden": {"total": n, "machines": {"<machine name>": n}}}`, where `hidden` counts what was left out. |
| `series` | `read` | Shows numbers over time for a service (`id`), or for a machine's own disks, memory and processor (`machine`). |
| `processes` | `read` | Shows a machine's newest process list (`machine` is its id or name): `sort`, `q`, `pid`, `limit`. |
| `process_history` | `read` | Shows the top 10 processes by memory or processor kept for a machine over up to 24 hours: `kind`, `from`, `to`. |
| `day` | `read` | Shows the last 24 hours in half hours: for each machine whether something was down, needed a look, or nothing happened, or it was not heard from, and the issues that opened. |
| `releases` | `read` | Lists the program releases the server holds and whether each is complete. |
| `certificate` | `read` | Shows the certificates the server serves itself. |
| `alert_settings` | `read` | Shows the alert settings. Addresses, user names and secrets are only `set` or `not set`. |
| `alert_suggestions` | `read` | Lists issues that keep opening, which the daily digest could take instead. |
| `logs` | `read-logs` | Searches log lines. |
| `archives` | `read-logs` | Lists the archived months of logs that can be loaded back. |
| `snooze` | `act` | Snoozes an issue until a time. |
| `unsnooze` | `act` | Wakes a snoozed issue. |
| `acknowledge` | `act` | Marks an issue as seen. |
| `note` | `act` | Adds a note to an issue. |
| `bulk` | `act` | Snoozes, unsnoozes or acknowledges many issues. |
| `watch` | `act` | Starts watching a service. |
| `unwatch` | `act` | Stops watching a service. |
| `routing` | `act` | Sets where a service's issues go, one channel or a list of channels for `down` and for `degraded`. A field that is not given stays as it was. |
| `machine_routing` | `act` | Sets how a machine that stops reporting is announced: `down`, one channel or a list, and `night`. A field that is not given stays as it was. |
| `hold` | `act` | Holds a service at a version. |
| `accept_proposal` | `act` | Accepts a found service or port. A hidden one can be named by id; `all` takes only what `proposals` shows unless `system` is true. |
| `dismiss_proposal` | `act` | Dismisses a proposal, with the same rule for `all` and `system`. |
| `keep_messages` | `act` | Keeps or stops keeping the text of a service's errors. |
| `set_job_timing` | `act` | Sets when a job counts as late and as run too long. A field left out stays as it was; an empty one clears it. |
| `scan_machine` | `act` | Asks an enrolled machine to look itself over again and send what it finds to proposals. Nothing found is watched until accepted. |
| `plan_downtime` | `act` | Says an enrolled machine is going down on purpose for a length of time (`for`, such as `15m`, at most `4h`; optional `reason`): no issue opens and nothing is sent for the machine going silent or its checks failing until the time is up. A second call replaces the window; `for` of `0` ends it. |
| `end_downtime` | `act` | Ends a machine's planned downtime now. |
| `downtime_schedules` | `read` | A machine's scheduled planned downtime: each with `id`, `repeat`, `at`, `time`, `days`, `for_seconds`, `reason`, `by` and `next`. |
| `schedule_downtime` | `act` | Schedules planned downtime that the server starts by itself: `repeat` of `once` (with `at`, an RFC 3339 time), `daily` or `weekly` (with `time`, such as `02:00`, in the night time zone, and for `weekly` `days`, 1 for Monday to 7 for Sunday), `for` (such as `30m`, at most `4h`) and an optional `reason`. A window it starts is not ended early when the machine comes back. |
| `remove_scheduled_downtime` | `act` | Removes a scheduled planned downtime, by the `schedule` id from `downtime_schedules`. |
| `add_rule` | `admin` | Adds an alert rule. |
| `update_rule` | `admin` | Changes an alert rule. A field left out stays as it was; an empty one clears it. |
| `delete_rule` | `admin` | Deletes an alert rule. |
| `set_checks` | `admin` | Replaces the checks added in the interface. |
| `allow_restart` | `admin` | Allows or forbids restarting a service. |
| `keys` | `admin` | Lists keys and tokens, never their text. |
| `make_key` | `admin` | Makes a key. Its text is returned once. |
| `revoke_key` | `admin` | Revokes a key. |
| `people` | `admin` | Lists the people who can sign in. |
| `add_person` | `admin` | Adds a person. |
| `remove_person` | `admin` | Removes a person. |
| `update_program` | `admin` | Asks an enrolled machine to fetch the newer `dokkit` program. |
| `update_machine` | `admin` | Asks the updater on a machine to move to a release the server holds completely. |
| `update_all` | `admin` | The same for every machine that has an updater. |
| `set_certificate` | `admin` | Puts a certificate for a real name in place. |
| `remove_certificate` | `admin` | Removes the uploaded certificate. |
| `certificate_settings` | `admin` | Shows the settings for getting and renewing the uploaded certificate. |
| `set_certificate_settings` | `admin` | Changes those settings. A setting left out stays as it was. |
| `renew_certificate` | `admin` | Gets a certificate now from the certificate authority. |
| `add_app` | `admin` | Adds an app that runs on many machines. Its key is returned once. |
| `add_dependency` | `admin` | Adds something outside that is depended on. With a check (`http` url or `tcp` address) it is put on an enrolled machine whose program runs the check; without one it belongs to the group Outside. |
| `add_job` | `admin` | Adds a job to watch. Its key and addresses are returned once. |
| `set_alert_settings` | `admin` | Changes alert settings. A setting left out stays as it was; an empty secret clears it. If the address a secret goes to changes (`ntfy_url`, `smtp_host`), send the secret again in the same call or it is cleared, and the answer says so. |
| `alert_people` | `read` | Lists the people alerts can be told with their own destinations. The ntfy address, Pushover key and routing key are only set or not set. |
| `alert_who` | `read` | Lists who is told at each level where someone is named. |
| `set_alert_person` | `admin` | Changes a person's destinations. A field not given stays; an empty one clears it. |
| `set_alert_who` | `admin` | Names who is told at one level (`default`, `rule`, `service` or `check`): person ids, or `["everyone"]`. |
| `test_alert` | `admin` | Sends a test alert by one channel, or to one person's destination with `person`. Answers sent, or one fixed reason. Four at once for each token, then one every 25 seconds; a page, or a push through PagerDuty, stays open for two minutes and then resolves itself, and costs twice as much (two at once, then one every 50 seconds). |
| `accept_suggestion` | `admin` | Sends a service's issues to the daily digest from now on. |
| `dismiss_suggestion` | `admin` | Dismisses an alert suggestion. |
| `restore_archive` | `admin` | Loads an archived month of logs back for a week. |

## Rules

- **Log contents have their own scope.** A token can be given everything except what is written in the logs.
- **A new token has no `act` scope** unless it is asked for.
- **Read tools are marked read-only**, so a client can run them without asking each time. `admin` tools are marked destructive.
- **What comes back is data.** Names, titles, notes, error text, deploy fields and output were written by machines and apps. Every answer starts with a line that says so.
- **Arguments are checked against the types the tool declares.** A wrong type is an `isError` answer, not a failure. A `null` argument is the same as one left out, and a whole number written as `5.0` is an integer. To clear a route, send an empty text.
- **Lists page by cursor.** The list tools (`find`, `jobs`, `job_runs`, `logs`, `errors`, `machines`, `issues`, `deploys`, `rules`, `proposals`, `keys`, `people`, `releases`) take the filters of their API list, `cursor` and `limit` (1 to 500, default 100). A list that fits one page answers as an array, as before; a longer one, or any call with `cursor` or `limit`, answers `{"items": [...], "next": "<cursor or null>"}`. `issues` takes `state` (`open`, `snoozed`, `closed` or `all`). `errors` with an `id` pages the group's reports the same way. `accept_proposal` and `dismiss_proposal` take `ids` or `all`. `proposals` is the one list that always answers an object, so that `hidden` has a place; it takes `system` (boolean) to include the operating system's own findings.
- **A token with `admin` can do through MCP everything a person can do in the interface,** except pairing phones, which carries a key that must not pass through an AI tool, and moving and deleting log lines of a service (`POST /services/<id>/logs/move` and `/logs/delete`), destructive actions that are the API's alone. Making such a token asks for confirmation in Settings.

## Built so far

`POST /mcp` with a user token: every tool in the table, 70 in all (25 `read`, 2 `read-logs`, 14 `act`, 29 `admin`), one for each call of the API a token can make. Making a full-control token, pairing and removing phones (`/phones`), moving log lines between services and the browser's own sign-in have no tool: they are Settings and the browser only. A tool the token may not use is not listed.


# `dokkit.toml`

One file in an app's repo that says what the app is and how to tell if it is healthy. It ships with the app.

```toml
schema = 1

[service]
id = "upload-portal"
name = "Upload portal"
kind = "service"                # service, job, dependency or app
environment = "production"      # anything else never alerts
version_from = "stats"          # "stats", a file path, or a command

[[check]]
type = "http"
url = "http://localhost:8080/healthz"
every = "30s"
timeout = "5s"
slow = "2s"                     # an answer slower than this is degraded, not down; http only, above 0, below timeout
fail_after = 3                  # bad results in a row before an issue opens; 1 to 100, default 3

[stats]
url = "http://localhost:8080/internal/stats"
key_env = "DOKKIT_STATS_KEY"     # the name of the variable, never the secret; must start with DOKKIT_STATS_

[logs]
path = "logs/*.jsonl"

[[job]]
id = "nightly-purge"
schedule = "0 1 * * *"
grace = "30m"                  # how late it may start; 30m when left out
max_runtime = "1h"              # how long a run may take; 1h when left out

[alert]
down = "page"                   # a suggested default only
degraded = "push"
```

## Sections

| Section | Holds |
|---|---|
| `schema` | The version of this file format. `1`. |
| `[service]` | What the app is. `id` is unique on its machine and never changes. |
| `[[check]]` | One per check. `type` is one of `http`, `tcp`, `process`, `windows-service`, `systemd`, `beat`, `job`, `stats`, `threshold`, `expiry` and `custom`. Each type has its own fields: `url` for `http` (an optional `status` is the answer that counts as healthy: a code such as `200`, a range such as `"200-299"`, or a list of those such as `[200, "400-403"]`, from 100 to 599; any other answer is down; without it anything under 400 is healthy; redirects are followed unless `status` includes a 3xx code), `port` for `tcp` (with an optional `host`, `localhost` when left out), `name` for `process` (the program's file name; an optional `command_has` also needs a piece of its text, ignoring case: the full executable path on Windows (as the system names it, after the drive: \Device\HarddiskVolumeN\..., so match from the folder, not the drive letter), the whole command line on Linux and macOS, so `command_has = '\envs\imageresizer\'` tells one app's `python.exe` from the rest, a backslash and a slash count the same, and a process that cannot be inspected does not match; an optional `at_least = 30` is the fewest matching processes that is healthy: fewer is `degraded`, none is `down`, and the value reported is how many were found, which is how an app that runs as dozens of worker processes is watched; see Which processes can be seen), `windows-service` and `systemd` (the unit), `metric` and `limit` for `threshold` (bad when the metric is over the limit), `date_from` for `expiry` (an `https` address or `host:port` for a certificate, or a file whose first line is a date; the check is `degraded` from 30 days before the date, counted in exact time, and `down` once it has passed, and shows the days left rounded up). All take `every` and `fail_after`, the number of bad results in a row (a whole number from 1 to 100, 3 when left out) after which the server opens an issue. `http` also takes `slow`: an answer that comes back successfully but takes longer is `degraded`, with the time as its value, and the server opens an issue only after its usual run of bad results. |
| `[stats]` | Where the stats document is and which environment variable holds its key. |
| `[logs]` | Files to read. Paths are relative to the file and must stay inside its folder. Each line is a JSON object (`t`, `level`, `msg`, `service`, `fields`) or a CLEF line; any other line is kept as its message. |
| `[[job]]` | A scheduled job: when it should run, how late it may be (`grace`, 30 minutes when left out), and how long it may take (`max_runtime`, 1 hour when left out). `schedule` is a five-field cron line read as UTC, and `@reboot` is refused. |
| `[alert]` | A starting suggestion for who is told. |

## Rules

**The file owns what the app is and how to check it. The interface owns who is told, snoozes and overrides.** The interface shows a file-declared check as coming from the file, and it is changed by changing the file. `[alert]` only seeds the routing the first time the service appears.

**Secrets never go in the file.** A field ending in `_env` names an environment variable that holds one.

**A declared check is active straight away.**

## How the file reaches Dokkit

Two ways, both supported:

1. **`dokkit` reads it.** `dokkit`'s own configuration lists the folders it may read `dokkit.toml` files from. That configuration is only editable by an administrator. `dokkit` re-reads a file when it changes.
2. **It is sent.** `dokkit apply` sends the file from anywhere that has a key, for example from CI. A machine key may declare any service on its machine. An app key may declare only the service it belongs to: `[service] id` must match, the machine and kind stay as they are, `[service]` may set the name and environment, `[[job]]` keeps `id`, `schedule`, `grace` and `max_runtime`, `[[check]]` may be of type `beat` or `custom` only (any other type is refused), and the other sections are dropped.

## Which processes can be seen

A `process` check sees the processes of every account, with no administrator rights, on each system, and matches by the program's file name (and `command_has` against the text below).

- **Windows.** The list of processes comes from a system snapshot, which includes other accounts' processes. The executable path used by `command_has` is asked of the system by process number, without opening the process, so Local Service sees other accounts' processes and their paths (`procs_windows.go`). A protected system process may give no path; it then matches by name only.
- **Linux.** `/proc/<pid>/comm` and `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` are readable by any user, so an unprivileged account sees all processes and their command lines. Where `/proc` is mounted with `hidepid=1` or `hidepid=2`, an account outside the allowed group sees only its own, and a process that is not listed is counted as not running. The program name is the kernel's, cut to 15 characters. The executable path (`/proc/<pid>/exe`) is not used, because only the owner or root can read it.
- **macOS.** `ps -axww` lists every user's processes with their command lines for any account, so the same applies as on Linux without `hidepid`.

## Checking it

`dokkit check` validates the file, runs every check once on the current machine, and prints exactly what would be sent. It needs no server. It refuses what the server refuses when the file is declared: `service.id` outside lower-case letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores (starting with a letter or digit), a `service.kind` that is not `service`, `job`, `dependency` or `app`, a check type that is not known, a job without an `id`, a job `schedule` that is not a cron line (five fields read as UTC, or `@hourly`, `@daily`, `@weekly`, `@monthly`, `@yearly`; `@reboot` is refused), and a `fail_after` that is not a whole number from 1 to 100. It also refuses a `key_env` that does not start with `DOKKIT_STATS_`, a `[stats] url` that is not an `http` or `https` address, and a `[logs] path` that leaves the file's folder. `dokkit watch` keeps a file with one of those last three and reports the part that cannot work. `spec/declare-cases.json` holds files both the program and the server's declare are tested against.


# The `dokkit` command line

One program on each watched machine, also used in an app's repo. `dokkit help` prints this list and `dokkit help <command>` says more about one.


## In an app's repo


### `dokkit init`

Asks what the app is and writes dokkit.toml. Asks a few questions and writes a dokkit.toml in this folder: what the app is, and how to tell it is healthy. Nothing is sent.


### `dokkit check [dokkit.toml]`

Runs the checks it can once and prints what would be sent. Checks the file's schema, service id and each check's fields. Runs the http, tcp, process, windows-service, systemd and expiry checks that can run here, once, and prints exactly what would be sent. Checks the app reports itself are listed as not run. A check aimed at another host does make its request. Needs no server and sends nothing to it. A slow answer shows as slow, not as a failure.


### `dokkit apply [dokkit.toml]`

Sends the file to the server. Declares the file to the server, for a file dokkit watch does not read. It needs this machine's key from dokkit enrol; the server refuses an app key. Sending the same file twice changes nothing.


## Jobs


### `dokkit run [--service <slug>] --job <name> -- <command> [arguments]`

Runs a command and reports how it went. Runs the command and reports its start, finish, exit code, duration and last lines of output. Exits with the command's own exit code. With this machine's key, a job declared in a dokkit.toml in the folders of the saved configuration is found by name, and --service says which service when it is not. With an app key, --service is ignored.


### `dokkit ping [--service <slug>] <name> [start|ok|fail]`

Reports a job that cannot be wrapped. Reports one event for a job: start, ok (the default) or fail.


## This machine


### `dokkit enrol <address> <token> [sha256:<certificate fingerprint>]`

Joins this machine to a server. Trades a one-time token for this machine's key and saves it. Given a fingerprint, it trusts the certificate with that fingerprint and no other.


### `dokkit status`

What this machine watches and when it last reported. Shows the files dokkit watch reads, when it last sent, and how many reports are waiting, and any folder it cannot read. It says a watch is running only while that watch has written down in the last three minutes, and then gives its process number. On Linux it shows the installed service when root, or the dokkit group, can read its files; the service's status itself can be read only with sudo.


### `dokkit doctor`

A rough check of the server and the clock. Says whether the server answers and knows this key, whether this machine's clock is within 30 seconds of the server's (a slow answer counts as clock difference, up to 10 seconds), and whether reports are waiting. A certificate that is not the one saved at enrol shows as the server not answering.


## Finding things


### `dokkit scan [--no-services] [--no-ports] [--no-tasks] [--no-containers] [--no-sites] [--no-disks] [--no-declarations]`

Looks over this machine and writes a proposal file. Lists what is on the machine that could be watched and writes it to dokkit-proposal.json in this folder. Sends nothing. Each --no- flag leaves one kind of thing out.


### `dokkit propose`

Sends the proposal file to be accepted. Sends dokkit-proposal.json, which a scan wrote. Nothing in it is watched until a person accepts it in the interface, or a token allowed to act accepts it through the API.


## Staying running


### `dokkit watch [--background]`

Watches this machine, as an ordinary program. Reads dokkit.toml files from the folders in DOKKIT_FOLDERS or in the saved configuration, and from the folders directly inside them. Runs their checks, sends the log files they name, runs the tasks a person accepted, and says the machine is alive once a minute. No administrator, no service. --background leaves it running after this window closes. Run like this, it never restarts a service or unit; only the installed service does.


### `dokkit folder add|remove <path>`

Sets which folders dokkit watch reads dokkit.toml files from. Adds a folder to the list dokkit watch reads dokkit.toml files from, or takes one out. It reads the dokkit.toml in the folder and in the folders directly inside it. The path is made absolute, and for add the folder must exist. Adding one twice changes nothing. A running watch picks up the change within a minute, with no restart. When the service is installed this changes the service's list, which needs an administrator, or root on Linux, and it prints the exact line to run. Otherwise it changes your own list. On Linux, it warns when the dokkit user cannot read the folder.


### `dokkit folder list`

Shows those folders. Lists the folders dokkit watch reads dokkit.toml files from: the installed service's when there is one, otherwise your own, and any it cannot read.


### `dokkit imessage on|off|status`

Lets this Mac send iMessages when the server asks. Alerts by iMessage go out through a Mac that is signed in to Messages. Nothing is sent unless this Mac was told it may: on records that it may, off takes it back, and status says which. Off is the default, and on works on a Mac only. A running dokkit watch picks the change up with no restart. When the service is installed this changes the service's configuration, which needs an administrator, or root, and it prints the exact line to run.


### `dokkit imessage test <recipient> [words...]`

Sends one iMessage from this Mac now, to prove Messages works. Sends the words, or a short test message, to a phone number or an email address through Messages on this Mac, without the server, and prints sent to <recipient> or the reason it was not. It works whether or not on was run. The first send makes macOS ask once, on this Mac's screen, whether dokkit may control Messages; allow it, or switch it on under System Settings, Privacy & Security, Automation. macOS remembers the answer only for a signed build of dokkit. A message is cut at 1000 characters.


### `dokkit startup on|off`

Starts dokkit watch each time you sign in. Windows only. Works on Windows only so far. Adds dokkit watch --background to your own startup programs, or takes it out. No administrator. On Linux, use dokkit service, or add dokkit watch --background to your desktop's startup programs. On macOS, add it to a launchd job.


### `dokkit service install|uninstall|update|start|stop`

Runs it as a service, on Windows or Linux. Needs an administrator or root. Works on Windows and on Linux with systemd; not on macOS yet. Installs dokkit as a service that starts with the machine, so it keeps watching with nobody signed in. On Windows it runs as Local Service, an account with no rights of its own, and reads only what that account can read, which leaves out other people's profile folders. On Linux it runs as a user named dokkit, which is made if useradd is there, and it reads only the folders that user can read. It may restart only the services or units that this machine's own configuration names, and only where the machine lets its account: on Windows the service's own permissions, on Linux root or systemd. On Windows it keeps to Program Files\DokkitProgram and ProgramData\DokkitProgram, and install refuses a data folder that holds anything but config.json, spool, dokkit.log and update. A program installed in the older Program Files\Dokkit and ProgramData\dokkit is moved by install or update: its config.json, spool and dokkit.log are copied, the service is pointed at the new copy, and the old files are left where they are. Needs an administrator prompt on Windows and root on Linux. On Linux, run through sudo, it uses the enrolment of the account that ran sudo, and root's own when that account has none, and says which file it used. update puts this copy in place of the installed one and restarts the service. uninstall leaves the machine enrolled on the server.


### `dokkit updater install|uninstall|run|status`

Updates the program, and the server on the machine that runs it, when asked. Windows only so far. Windows only so far. install, from an administrator prompt, once: copies this program to Program Files\DokkitUpdater, makes ProgramData\DokkitUpdater for administrators and the system account only, registers the scheduled task Dokkit updater (system account, every five minutes and at start-up), and runs one check. It needs the program's service installed first. run is what the task runs: it asks the server whether this machine has been told to move to a version, and only installs a release whose list is signed with the project's release key and whose files match it. It never installs an older version. status prints the installed versions, the last check and the last result. uninstall removes the task and the copied file.


## This machine


### `dokkit version`

Prints the version of this build. Prints the version this build was made as, such as v1.2.3. A build made by hand says v0.0.0-dev.


## Tasks


### `dokkit task list`

The tasks on this machine and whether each is accepted. Lists the tasks in this folder and in the folders this machine reads. When the server answers, says of each whether it is accepted, not accepted yet, or changed since it was accepted. When it lists any tasks, says which account you are running as.


### `dokkit task run <name>`

Runs a task here to try it. Runs the task on this machine now. The server can only ask for a task a person accepted, pinned to the exact command accepted.


## Trying it with no server

```
$ dokkit check
dokkit.toml: upload-portal, 2 check(s)
  ok   http           http://localhost:8080/healthz
       would send {"at":"2026-10-06T22:08:58.1420895Z","check":"http","service":"upload-portal","state":"ok","type":"state","value":10}
  ok   tcp            port 5432
       would send {"at":"2026-10-06T22:08:58.1432929Z","check":"tcp","service":"upload-portal","state":"ok","type":"state","value":1}
```


# The Dokkit API

Dokkit watches machines, services and jobs. This is the HTTP API that the `dokkit` program, the command line, the client libraries, the MCP server and any script use.

Every call carries a key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Key prefixes: `dke_` enrolment token, `dkm_` machine key, `dka_` app key (write only), `dku_` user token with the scopes `read`, `read-logs`, `act`, `admin`.


## Intake

Machines and apps send reports, deploys and declarations. Machine key or app key.


### POST /api/v1/enrol

Trade an enrolment token for a machine key. Spends a one-use enrolment token and makes the machine. The answer holds the machine key, shown once. A name that is already enrolled answers 409 and the token is kept, unless the token was made for that machine; then it enrols again and revokes that machine's earlier keys. Takes no key in the header. The enrolment token (`dke_`) goes in the body.


Send:

```
{
  "token": "dke_3kQ9xV2mTn7LwRb8",
  "hostname": "db-01",
  "os": "windows",
  "arch": "amd64",
  "dokkit": "0.1.0"
}
```

`200` The machine and its key.

```json
{
  "machine": "6f1c2a8e-3b7d-4c52-9e0a-5d41b7c8e9f3",
  "key": "dkm_7Hq2pXz4Yc9VnB1a"
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`409` Conflict.

`422` The body does not fit.

### POST /api/v1/report

Send a batch of lines. The main door. The body is newline-delimited JSON, one item per line, with a `type` and an `at` or `t`. The types are `state`, `inventory`, `metric`, `beat`, `job`, `stats`, `log`, `deploy` and `custom`. A batch is at most 5 MB compressed and 10,000 lines. A refused line does not fail the batch. Send the same `Dokkit-Batch` id again and nothing is stored twice. An app key may not send `state` or `inventory`, and may make 100 checks per service. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`) or an app key (`dka_`).

- `Dokkit-Batch` (header, optional): Names the batch. Sending it again stores nothing twice.
- `Content-Encoding` (header, optional): Set to gzip when the body is compressed.

Send:

```
{"type":"job","service":"nightly-purge","name":"nightly-purge","run":"r-2041","event":"ok","exit_code":0,"duration_ms":81234}
{"type":"log","t":"2026-10-05T21:14:03.120Z","level":"error","msg":"Upload failed","service":"upload-portal","fields":{"route":"/upload","status":500}}

```

`200` How many lines were accepted, and the ones refused.

```json
{
  "accepted": 1,
  "refused": [
    {
      "line": 2,
      "code": "unknown_service",
      "message": "No service \"upload-portal\" on this machine."
    }
  ]
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`413` Too large.

`422` The batch id is not a UUID (`bad_batch`), or the body is not valid gzip (`bad_gzip`).

`429` An app key has used up its bucket of 10,000 lines, refilling at 100 a second. Wait for Retry-After seconds.

### GET /api/v1/in/{key}/job/{name}/{event}

Ping a job with a web request. For anything that can only make a web request, such as a cron job on a storage box. `start`, `ok` and `fail` record the run. Any other event answers 404. Takes an app key (`dka_`).

- `key` (path): An app key (`dka_`). It travels in the address because the callers can only make a web request.
- `name` (path): The job's name.
- `event` (path): What happened.
- `run` (query, optional): Ties a start to its finish.

`200` Recorded.

```json
{
  "ok": true
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`404` Not found.

`413` Too large.

`422` The body does not fit.

`429` An app key has used up its bucket of 10,000 lines, refilling at 100 a second. Wait for Retry-After seconds.

### POST /api/v1/in/{key}/job/{name}/{event}

Ping a job and keep its output. Same as the GET. The body, if there is one, is kept as the last lines of the job's output, at most 16 KB. Any content type is accepted. Takes an app key (`dka_`).

- `key` (path): An app key (`dka_`). It travels in the address because the callers can only make a web request.
- `name` (path): The job's name.
- `event` (path): What happened.
- `run` (query, optional): Ties a start to its finish.

Send:

```
Purged 412 files.
Done.

```

`200` Recorded.

```json
{
  "ok": true
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`404` Not found.

`413` Too large.

`422` The body does not fit.

`429` An app key has used up its bucket of 10,000 lines, refilling at 100 a second. Wait for Retry-After seconds.

### PUT /api/v1/declare

Declare a service from a dokkit.toml. The contents of a `dokkit.toml`, sent as JSON with the same structure. Sending the same file twice changes nothing. Checks, jobs, logs and stats become active. Tasks become proposals. The file owns the service and its checks, so checks it no longer lists are removed. Only a machine key may declare; an app key answers 403. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`).


Send:

```
{
  "schema": 1,
  "service": {
    "id": "upload-portal",
    "name": "Upload portal",
    "kind": "service"
  },
  "check": [
    {
      "type": "http",
      "name": "front-page",
      "url": "http://localhost:8080/health",
      "expect": 200
    }
  ]
}
```

`200` The service id.

```json
{
  "service": "6f1c2a8e-3b7d-4c52-9e0a-5d41b7c8e9f3"
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

`422` The body does not fit.

### GET /api/v1/ping

Check the address, the key and the clock. Lets a machine check its address, its key and its clock. The answer holds the server's time. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`) or an app key (`dka_`).


`200` The key works.

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "time": "2026-10-05T21:14:03.120000Z"
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

### POST /api/v1/proposals

Send what a scan found. What `dokkit scan` found, as the file was written. Nothing in it is active until a person accepts it in the interface. So far the server keeps running Windows services and listening ports, and leaves out what is already watched or was dismissed. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`).


Send:

```
{
  "os": "windows",
  "found": {
    "services": [
      {
        "name": "Spooler",
        "display": "Print Spooler",
        "state": "running"
      }
    ],
    "ports": [
      {
        "port": 5432,
        "program": "postgres.exe"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

`200` How many things from this machine now wait.

```json
{
  "waiting": 2
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`422` The body does not fit.

### POST /api/v1/deploys

Record a deploy from CI. For CI. `host` is the machine the version went onto, when that is not the machine the service lives on. A deploy is also recorded when a service's reported version changes, so most apps never call this. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`) or an app key (`dka_`).


Send:

```
{
  "service": "upload-portal",
  "version": "2.3.0",
  "host": "web-02",
  "commit": "abc123",
  "by": "ci"
}
```

`200` Recorded.

```json
{
  "ok": true
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`422` The body does not fit.

`429` An app key has used up its bucket of 10,000 lines, refilling at 100 a second. Wait for Retry-After seconds.

### GET /api/v1/checks

Get the checks added in the interface. The checks added in the interface for this machine, for the `dokkit` program to run. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`).


`200` The checks.

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "service": "spooler",
      "name": "windows-service",
      "type": "windows-service",
      "config": {
        "name": "Spooler"
      },
      "restart": false
    }
  ]
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

## Errors

Error reports from an app, in Dokkit's own format or as Sentry envelopes. App key.


### POST /api/v1/errors

Report an error in Dokkit's format. One error report. Reports are grouped by `type` and the app's own frames. Message text is dropped unless the service's page is set to keep it. An error does not open an issue or alert anyone. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`) or an app key (`dka_`).


Send:

```
{
  "at": "2026-10-05T21:14:03.120Z",
  "service": "upload-portal",
  "release": "2.3.0",
  "environment": "production",
  "host": "web-02",
  "type": "TimeoutError",
  "handled": true,
  "frames": [
    {
      "file": "app/worker.py",
      "function": "run_job",
      "line": 212,
      "own": true
    }
  ],
  "tags": {
    "route": "/upload",
    "status": "500"
  }
}
```

`200` Recorded.

```json
{
  "ok": true
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`422` The body does not fit.

`429` An app key has used up its bucket of 10,000 lines, refilling at 100 a second. Wait for Retry-After seconds.

### POST /api/{project}/envelope

Report errors from a Sentry SDK. The door for Sentry's open-source SDKs. An SDK is given an address made from an app key and Dokkit's host. Error events are stored; everything else is read and dropped, and the answer tells the SDK to stop sending those kinds. Gzip is accepted. The app key is read from the `X-Sentry-Auth` header, the `sentry_key` query value, or the envelope's first line. The `project` segment is whatever the SDK was given and is not used. Takes an app key (`dka_`).

- `project` (path): The project part of the address the SDK built.
- `sentry_key` (query, optional): The app key, when the SDK sends it in the query.
- `X-Sentry-Auth` (header, optional): Holds `sentry_key=<app key>` among its fields.
- `Content-Encoding` (header, optional): Set to gzip when the body is compressed.

Send:

```
{"event_id":"9ec79c33ec9942ab8353589fcb2e04dc","dsn":"https://dka_4Rm8@your.domain.com/1"}
{"type":"event"}
{"exception":{"values":[{"type":"TimeoutError","value":"upload timed out"}]},"release":"2.3.0"}

```

`200` Accepted. The `X-Sentry-Rate-Limits` header tells the SDK to stop sending kinds Dokkit drops.

```json
{}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`413` Too large.

`422` The body does not fit.

`429` An app key has used up its bucket of 10,000 lines, refilling at 100 a second. Wait for Retry-After seconds.

## Work

The `dokkit` program asks for tasks, sends their output and result, and fetches updates. Machine key.


### GET /api/v1/program/{target}

Download the newer dokkit program. The newer `dokkit` program this server holds, for a machine asked to fetch it. The target is the operating system and architecture, such as `windows-amd64`. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`).

- `target` (path): The kind of machine, as `<os>-<arch>`.

`200` The program file.

`401` Missing or bad key.

`404` Not found.

### GET /api/v1/work

Ask for a task to run. The `dokkit` program asks for work and the server holds the request for up to `wait` seconds. 204 means nothing to do; ask again. `command_sha256` is the pin of the task that was accepted; the program runs the task only when its own pin is the same one. A task has a name and nothing else. There are no arguments. The one exception is the built-in task `dokkit:imessage`, which is offered only to the Mac chosen for iMessage, has an empty `command_sha256`, needs no accepting, and carries two more fields: `to`, the recipients, and `text`, the message. The program answers it on the result address with `exit_code` 0 when every recipient was sent to, 1 otherwise, or `refused` with the reason, and posts one line of output for each recipient. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`).

- `wait` (query, optional): Seconds to hold the request.

`200` A task to run.

```json
{
  "run": "6f1c2a8e-3b7d-4c52-9e0a-5d41b7c8e9f3",
  "task": "nightly-purge",
  "as": "ordinary",
  "command_sha256": "9f2b6c0d1e7a4b83a5c6f1d2e3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d1e0f9a8b7c6d5e4f30"
}
```

`204` Nothing to do. Ask again.

`401` Missing or bad key.

### POST /api/v1/work/{run}/output

Send a chunk of task output. A chunk of the running task's output, as plain text. The server keeps the last part. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`).

- `run` (path): The run id from `GET /work`.

Send:

```
Purged 412 files.

```

`200` Kept.

```json
{
  "ok": true
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`404` Not found.

### POST /api/v1/work/{run}/result

Send the result of a task. Either an exit code with the duration, or a refusal with the reason. A refusal is how the program says it will not run a task that is not defined on its machine or not accepted. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`).

- `run` (path): The run id from `GET /work`.

Send:

```
{
  "exit_code": 0,
  "duration_ms": 81234
}
```

`200` Kept.

```json
{
  "ok": true
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`404` The run is not running on this machine, or the body is neither an exit code nor a refusal.

### GET /api/v1/tasks/accepted

List the tasks accepted for this machine. So `dokkit task list` can say which tasks are accepted. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`).


`200` The accepted tasks.

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "task": "nightly-purge",
      "command_sha256": "9f2b6c0d1e7a4b83a5c6f1d2e3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d1e0f9a8b7c6d5e4f30",
      "as": "ordinary"
    }
  ]
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

### GET /api/v1/releases/{version}/{file}

Download a release file. A file of a release, for the updater on a machine. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`).

- `version` (path): A release version. Letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores; not starting with a dot.
- `file` (path): A file name in that release, such as `SHA256SUMS`. Same characters as a version.

`200` The file.

`401` Missing or bad key.

`404` Not found.

### GET /api/v1/update

Ask which version to move to. The updater on a machine tells the server what is installed and asks whether to move. The server remembers the versions, that the machine has an updater, and whether it hosts the server. 204 when no version is wanted, the server does not hold the wanted version completely, or every part the machine has is already on it; otherwise 200 with the version. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`).

- `program` (query, optional): The installed program version.
- `server` (query, optional): The installed server version. Left out when the machine does not run the server.
- `updater` (query, optional): The installed updater version.
- `os` (query, optional): 
- `arch` (query, optional): 

`200` Move to this version.

```json
{
  "version": "v1.2.3"
}
```

`204` Nothing to do.

`401` Missing or bad key.

### POST /api/v1/update/result

Report how an update went. The server keeps the last result for the machine and clears its wanted version when `ok` is true. Takes a machine key (`dkm_`).


Send:

```
{
  "version": "v1.2.3",
  "ok": true,
  "note": "program, updater"
}
```

`200` Kept.

```json
{
  "ok": true
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`422` The input is not right.

## Read

Read issues, machines, services, jobs, logs, errors, deploys, rules, proposals and tasks. User token.


### GET /api/v1/proposals

List things waiting to be accepted. Found things and tasks that wait for a person to accept them. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `read` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.


`200` OK.

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "6f1c2a8e-3b7d-4c52-9e0a-5d41b7c8e9f3",
      "kind": "service",
      "name": "Spooler",
      "detail": {
        "label": "Print Spooler",
        "saw": "Running"
      },
      "machine": "db-01"
    }
  ],
  "next": null
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

### GET /api/v1/deploys

List deploys. Deploy history, newest first. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `read` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.


`200` OK.

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "service": "6f1c2a8e-3b7d-4c52-9e0a-5d41b7c8e9f3",
      "name": "Upload portal",
      "machine": "web-02",
      "version": "2.3.0",
      "from": "2.2.9",
      "commit": "abc123",
      "by": "ci",
      "how": "reported",
      "at": "2026-10-05T19:30:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "next": null
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

### GET /api/v1/errors

List error groups. Error groups by type and place, newest first, at most 200. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `read` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.


`200` OK.

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "6f1c2a8e-3b7d-4c52-9e0a-5d41b7c8e9f3",
      "type": "TimeoutError",
      "top": {
        "file": "app/worker.py",
        "function": "run_job",
        "line": 212,
        "own": true
      },
      "count": 14,
      "first_seen": "2026-10-05T19:40:00Z",
      "last_seen": "2026-10-05T21:14:03Z",
      "release": "2.3.0",
      "host": "web-02",
      "handled": true,
      "service": "6f1c2a8e-3b7d-4c52-9e0a-5d41b7c8e9f3",
      "name": "Upload portal",
      "machine": "web-02"
    }
  ],
  "next": null
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

### GET /api/v1/day

The last day. The last 24 hours in 48 half hours, for each machine, and the issues that opened in that time. The last cell is the half hour that holds `to`. A cell is `down` if an issue that was down overlapped it, else `degraded` if any issue overlapped it, else `quiet` if the machine was heard from, else `none` (no signal). An issue counts in the state it has now, for its whole life. Soon issues and issues of services that are not in production colour nothing. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `read` scope.

- `to` (query, optional): The end of the window, RFC 3339. Defaults to now.

`200` OK.

```json
{
  "from": "2026-01-09T12:30:00Z",
  "to": "2026-01-10T12:30:00Z",
  "machines": [
    {

      ]

      "closed_at": "2026-01-10T10:50:00Z"
    },

      "at": "2026-01-10T11:40:00Z",
      "title": "web-02: Disk C is nearly full",
      "machine": "web-02",
      "state": "degraded",
      "sent": "Pushed",
      "closed_at": null
    }
  ]
}
```

`422` to is not an RFC 3339 time.

### GET /api/v1/inbox

What needs a look. What needs a look, what will soon, what was found and is not watched, what is snoozed, issues in other environments, and how many things are fine. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `read` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.


`200` OK.

```json
{
  "needs_you": [
    {
      "id": "6f1c2a8e-3b7d-4c52-9e0a-5d41b7c8e9f3",
      "short_id": "DOK-12",
      "kind": "check",
      "state": "down",
      "title": "upload-portal is down",
      "note": "Connection refused",
      "count": 3,
      "since": "2026-10-05T20:41:00Z",
      "snoozed_until": null,
      "acknowledged_at": null,
      "machine": "web-02",
      "service": "6f1c2a8e-3b7d-4c52-9e0a-5d41b7c8e9f3",
```

### GET /api/v1/services/{id}/series

Get chart data for a service. Without `metric`, the names of the metrics the service has. With `metric`, its points between `from` and `to`. Answers 404 for an unknown service, a time that is not RFC 3339, or a `from` that is not before `to`. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `read` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.

- `id` (path): The id of the service.
- `metric` (query, optional): The metric's name.
- `from` (query, optional): Start, RFC 3339. Defaults to 24 hours before `to`.
- `to` (query, optional): End, RFC 3339. Defaults to now.
- `points` (query, optional): How many points.

`200` OK.

```json
{
  "metric": "queue_depth",
  "points": [
    {
      "at": "2026-10-05T20:00:00Z",
      "value": 4
    }
  ]
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

`404` Not found.

### GET /api/v1/logs

Search log lines. Log lines, newest first, at most 500. `level` is that level and worse. Answers 404 for an unknown machine or service, or a time that is not RFC 3339. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `read-logs` scope.

- `q` (query, optional): Search text.
- `level` (query, optional): That level and worse.
- `machine` (query, optional): A machine id or name.
- `service` (query, optional): A service id.
- `from` (query, optional): Start, RFC 3339.
- `to` (query, optional): End, RFC 3339.

`200` OK.

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "t": "2026-10-05T21:14:03.120Z",
      "level": "error",
      "msg": "Upload failed",
      "fields": {
        "route": "/upload",
        "status": 500
      },
      "machine": "web-02",
      "service": "upload-portal"
    }
  ],
  "next": null
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

`404` Not found.

### GET /api/v1/certificate

## Act

Snooze and acknowledge issues, route and hold services, accept found things, run tasks, keep error text and set when a job is late. User token with `act`.


### POST /api/v1/issues/{id}/snooze

Snooze an issue. Snoozes an issue until a time. An unknown issue answers 404. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `act` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.

- `id` (path): The id of the issue.

Send:

```
{
  "until": "2026-10-06T08:00:00Z"
}
```

`200` Done.

```json
{
  "ok": true
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

`404` Not found.

`422` The body does not fit.

### POST /api/v1/issues/{id}/unsnooze

Bring a snoozed issue back. Brings a snoozed issue back. An unknown issue answers 404. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `act` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.

- `id` (path): The id of the issue.

`200` Done.

```json
{
  "ok": true
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

`404` Not found.

### POST /api/v1/issues/{id}/acknowledge

Mark an issue as seen. Marks an issue as seen. An unknown issue answers 404. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `act` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.

- `id` (path): The id of the issue.

`200` Done.

```json
{
  "ok": true
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

`404` Not found.

### POST /api/v1/issues/{id}/notes

Add a note to an issue. Adds a note. The note is signed with the token's label. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `act` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.

- `id` (path): The id of the issue.

Send:

```
{
  "text": "Restarted the upload pool on web-02."
}
```

`200` Done.

```json
{
  "ok": true
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

`404` Not found.

`422` The body does not fit.

### POST /api/v1/issues/bulk

Snooze, unsnooze or acknowledge many issues. Does one action to a list of issue ids. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `act` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.


Send:

```
{
  "ids": [
    "6f1c2a8e-3b7d-4c52-9e0a-5d41b7c8e9f3"
  ],
  "action": "snooze",
  "until": "2026-10-06T08:00:00Z"
}
```

`200` Done.

```json
{
  "ok": true
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

`422` The body does not fit.

### POST /api/v1/services/{id}/watch

Start watching a found service. Starts watching a found service. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `act` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.

- `id` (path): The id of the service.

`200` The service after the change.

```json
{
  "id": "6f1c2a8e-3b7d-4c52-9e0a-5d41b7c8e9f3",
  "slug": "upload-portal",
  "name": "Upload portal",
```

### PUT /api/v1/services/{id}/routing

Set who is told about a service. Sets the channel for `down` and for `degraded`. A field that is not sent stays as it was; a value that is not a channel clears that route. `night` is optional; false holds the alerts of a night until it ends. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `act` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.

- `id` (path): The id of the service.

Send:

```
{
  "down": "page",
  "degraded": "digest",
  "night": false
}
```

`200` The routing now in force.

```json
{
  "down": "page",
  "degraded": "digest",
  "night": false
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

`404` Not found.

## Admin

Keys, people, alert rules and settings, interface-added checks, restart, making jobs, accepting tasks, updating the program and loading logs back. User token with `admin`.


### POST /api/v1/apps

Add an app that runs on many machines. Adds an app, such as a desktop program, that belongs to no one machine. Its key is returned once and goes into the app's build. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `admin` scope.


Send:

```
{
  "name": "Label printer"
}
```

`200` The app, with its key shown once.

```json
{
  "id": "5f0c1c0e-2a52-4c0f-9d5e-6f1b2f9a7c11",
  "name": "Label printer",
  "slug": "label-printer",
  "key": "dka_..."
}
```

`403` The key may not do this.

`422` The input is not right.

```json
    "ok": "https://your.domain.com/api/v1/in/dka_3f9c0d2e7b4a/job/weekly-report/ok",
    "fail": "https://your.domain.com/api/v1/in/dka_3f9c0d2e7b4a/job/weekly-report/fail"
```

### GET /api/v1/keys

List keys. Every key that still works, newest first. The key text is never shown again; `hint` is the start of it. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `admin` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.


`200` The keys.

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "6f1c2a8e-3b7d-4c52-9e0a-5d41b7c8e9f3",
      "kind": "user",
      "hint": "dku_7Hq2",
      "label": "ci-bot",
      "scopes": [
        "read",
        "act"
      ],
      "used_at": null,
      "expires_at": null,
      "inserted_at": "2026-10-05T19:00:00Z",
      "machine": null,
      "service": null
    }
  ],
  "next": null
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

### POST /api/v1/keys

Make a key. Makes a user token with a label and scopes (only scopes the calling token holds, and never `admin`, which is made in Settings), an app key for a service, or a one-use enrolment token that lasts an hour. The key is shown once, in this answer. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `admin` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.


Send:

```
{
  "kind": "user",
  "label": "ci-bot",
  "scopes": [
    "read",
    "act"
  ]
}
```

`200` The key, shown once.

```json
{
  "id": "6f1c2a8e-3b7d-4c52-9e0a-5d41b7c8e9f3",
  "key": "dku_7Hq2pXz4Yc9VnB1aQw3E"
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

`404` Not found.

`422` The body does not fit.

### POST /api/v1/tasks/{id}/accept

Send the command and pin that proposals shows. A task whose command or pin has changed since answers 422. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `admin` scope.   "system": false
```
}
```

```json
  "ok": true
}
```

### POST /api/v1/machines/{id}/update

Approve a release for a machine, or ask it to fetch the program. With `version`, sets the machine's wanted version, and only to a version the server holds completely (422 `not_held`, or `bad_version` when it is not `v` and three numbers). The updater on the machine does the rest. Without a body, asks an enrolled machine to fetch the newer `dokkit` program from this server, which a person finishes on the machine; 422 when the server holds no program. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `admin` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.

- `id` (path): The id of the machine.

Send:

```
{
  "version": "v1.2.3"
}
```

`200` Asked: the version; or the run id of the fetch.

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "version": "v1.2.3"
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

`404` Not found.

`422` The input is not right.

### PUT /api/v1/alerts

Change alert settings. Saves the settings that are sent and checks them. `imessage_machine` must be an enrolled machine whose os is darwin, and every recipient in `imessage_to` and `sms_to` a phone number (or, for iMessage, an email address); otherwise 422. Answers with the settings as they now are. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `admin` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.


Send:

```
{
  "down": "push",
  "pagerduty_key": "R0UT1NGKEY",
  "night_to": "8"
}
```

`200` The settings after the change.

```json
{
  "down": "push",
  "degraded": "push",
  "push_with": "ntfy",
  "disk_limit": "90",
  "memory_limit": "95",
  "night_from": "22",
  "night_to": "7",
  "night_offset": "0",
  "pagerduty_key": "set",
  "webhook_url": "set"
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

`422` The input is not right.

### POST /api/v1/alerts/test

Send a test alert. Sends a test alert by one channel. Answers ok, or 422 with one reason. For SMS it is Twilio's own message when it gave one, and for iMessage it is the Mac's answer, which is waited for up to a minute. For the others it is a fixed reason that never carries anything the far end said. A 422 with code `slow_down` comes after four tests at once for a token, then one every 25 seconds. Answers 422 too when the channel is not one that sends. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `admin` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.


Send:

```
{
  "channel": "webhook"
}
```

`200` Sent.

```json
{
  "ok": true
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

`422` The input is not right.

### POST /api/v1/logs/archives/{name}/restore

### PUT /api/v1/releases/{version}/{file}

Put a release file on the server. The body is the file, as is, up to 200 MB, and replaces a file of that name. It is written to disk as it arrives. The server stores it and does not check it; the updater does. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `admin` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.

- `version` (path): A release version. Letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores; not starting with a dot.
- `file` (path): A file name in that release, such as `SHA256SUMS`. Same characters as a version.

`200` Stored.

```json
{
  "ok": true
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

`413` The file is over 200 MB.

`422` The name is not allowed.

### DELETE /api/v1/releases/{version}

Remove a release. Removes every file of that version from the server. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `admin` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.

- `version` (path): A release version. Letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores; not starting with a dot.

`200` Removed.

```json
{
  "ok": true
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

`404` Not found.

`422` The name is not allowed.

### POST /api/v1/update-all

Ask every updater to move to a release. Sets the wanted version on every machine that has an updater. Only a version the server holds completely is accepted: 422 with code `not_held` otherwise, and `bad_version` when it is not `v` and three numbers. Nothing updates until this is called; there is no automatic following of new releases. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `admin` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.


Send:

```
{
  "version": "v1.2.3"
}
```

`200` Asked.

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "version": "v1.2.3",
  "machines": 3
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

`422` The version is not one the server holds completely.

### PUT /api/v1/certificate

Put a certificate in place. Checks that both parse, that the key belongs to the first certificate, that it is neither expired nor not yet valid and that it names at least one DNS name, then saves both and serves the certificate at once to clients that ask for one of its names (SNI). Anything else, and a client that connects by address, still gets the installed certificate. A server that does not serve TLS itself answers 422. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `admin` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.


Send:

```
{
  "cert": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----\n",
  "key": "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\n...\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----\n"
}
```

`200` The certificates after the change.

```json
{
  "installed": {
    "names": [
      "web-01"
    ],
    "issuer": "web-01",
    "not_after": "2036-10-01T13:00:00Z",
    "self_signed": true,
    "sha256": "a99f59d72d4fe3caf976fa019c671dc3e184b9f9c4e7b6ce4494e9c85df1ad3d"
  },
  "uploaded": {
    "names": [
      "example.dokkit.dev"
    ],
    "issuer": "R11",
    "not_after": "2027-01-19T13:00:00Z",
    "self_signed": false,
    "sha256": "069ea4a89410f21e10658bbdb91aa9555af7e39294d4c08e999c7765ddf0d390"
  }
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

`422` A check failed. The message says which.

### DELETE /api/v1/certificate

Remove the uploaded certificate. Removes the uploaded certificate. The installed one is not touched. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `admin` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.


`200` The certificates after the change.

```json
{
  "installed": {
    "names": [
      "web-01"
    ],
    "issuer": "web-01",
    "not_after": "2036-10-01T13:00:00Z",
    "self_signed": true,
    "sha256": "a99f59d72d4fe3caf976fa019c671dc3e184b9f9c4e7b6ce4494e9c85df1ad3d"
  },
  "uploaded": {
    "names": [
      "example.dokkit.dev"
    ],
    "issuer": "R11",
    "not_after": "2027-01-19T13:00:00Z",
    "self_signed": false,
    "sha256": "069ea4a89410f21e10658bbdb91aa9555af7e39294d4c08e999c7765ddf0d390"
  }
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

`422` A check failed. The message says which.

### GET /api/v1/certificate/settings

Settings for getting a certificate by itself. The name, the Cloudflare token (only as `set` or `not set`) and the certificate authority's directory. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `admin` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.


`200` The settings.

```json
{
  "acme_name": "example.dokkit.dev",
  "acme_cloudflare_token": "set",
  "acme_directory": "https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory"
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

### PUT /api/v1/certificate/settings

Change those settings. Once `acme_name` and `acme_cloudflare_token` are set, the server gets a certificate for the name from the certificate authority, proving the name with a TXT record at `_acme-challenge.<name>` that it adds at Cloudflare and removes again, and renews it when 30 days or fewer are left. A setting left out stays as it was. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `admin` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.


Send:

```
{
  "acme_name": "example.dokkit.dev",
  "acme_cloudflare_token": "cf-api-token"
}
```

`200` The settings after the change.

```json
{
  "acme_name": "example.dokkit.dev",
  "acme_cloudflare_token": "set",
  "acme_directory": "https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory"
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

`422` A setting is not right. The message says which.

### POST /api/v1/certificate/renew

Get a certificate now. Gets a certificate for `acme_name` now, whatever the one held has left. It waits for the whole exchange, which can take a few minutes. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `admin` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.


`200` The certificates after the change.

```json
{
  "installed": {
    "names": [
      "web-01"
    ],
    "issuer": "web-01",
    "not_after": "2036-10-01T13:00:00Z",
    "self_signed": true,
    "sha256": "a99f59d72d4fe3caf976fa019c671dc3e184b9f9c4e7b6ce4494e9c85df1ad3d"
  },
  "uploaded": {
    "names": [
      "example.dokkit.dev"
    ],
    "issuer": "R11",
    "not_after": "2027-01-19T13:00:00Z",
    "self_signed": false,
    "sha256": "069ea4a89410f21e10658bbdb91aa9555af7e39294d4c08e999c7765ddf0d390"
  },
  "renewal": {
    "at": "2026-12-20T03:00:00Z",
    "ok": true,
    "note": "Renewed, runs out 2027-03-20"
  }
}
```

`401` Missing or bad key.

`403` The key may not do this.

`422` It failed. The message says why; the same sentence is kept as `renewal` in `GET /certificate`.

## MCP

The MCP server for AI tools. User token.


### GET /mcp

Not served. Answers 405. The MCP server takes POST only. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `read` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.


`401` Missing or bad key.

`405` Method not allowed.

### POST /mcp

Talk to the MCP server. The MCP server, as JSON-RPC over one POST address. It can do no more than the user token allows. An AI tool with a token can do through MCP everything the token can do through the API. The tools are, with `read` scope: `attention`, `find`, `service`, `jobs`, `job_runs`, `errors`, `since_deploy`, `tasks`, `machines`, `machine`, `issues`, `issue`, `deploys`, `versions`, `rules`, `proposals`, `task_runs`, `series` and `day`; with `read-logs` scope: `logs`; with `act` scope: `snooze`, `acknowledge`, `unsnooze`, `note`, `bulk`, `watch`, `unwatch`, `routing`, `hold`, `accept_proposal`, `dismiss_proposal` and `run_task`; with `admin` scope: `add_rule`, `update_rule`, `delete_rule`, `set_checks`, `allow_restart`, `keys`, `make_key`, `revoke_key`, `people`, `add_person` and `remove_person`. `make_key` returns the key text once. Admin tools are marked destructive. `tools/list` shows only the tools the token may use. Every answer starts with a line saying that what follows is data written by machines and apps, never instructions. An argument of the wrong type is an `isError` answer; a null argument is the same as one left out, and a whole number written as 5.0 is an integer. A tool error is an answer with `isError` true, not an HTTP error. Takes a user token (`dku_`) with the `read` scope. Without `read-logs`, job output, task output, error messages and notes are left out of the answer.


Send:

```
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "find",
    "arguments": {
      "q": "upload",
      "machine": "web-02"
    }
  }
}
```

`200` A JSON-RPC answer, with a result or an error.

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "result": {
    "content": [
      {
        "type": "text",
        "text": "[{\"id\":\"6f1c2a8e-3b7d-4c52-9e0a-5d41b7c8e9f3\",\"name\":\"Upload portal\",\"state\":\"ok\"}]"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

`202` A notification, which has no id and gets no answer.

`400` The body is not a request.

`401` Missing or bad key.
